Fit the initial hazard models

Source: R/fit-initial.R
fit_initial.Rd

Fits the initial (nuisance) hazard model for each event process (Cox models, or HAL), and the baseline treatment model if requested, and expands the data to the grid of all observed event times up to tau. It also builds the discrete product state space of the processes that other processes' hazards depend on. The result is the input to tmle_estimate() and intervention_curve().

Usage

fit_initial(
  data,
  models,
  tau,
  censoring = "censoring",
  treatment_model = NULL,
  arms = NULL,
  max_count = 1,
  control = list(),
  hal_control = list(),
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame of observed event history data in long format, with one row per event and columns id, time and event (the name of the process that jumped), plus any baseline covariates used in models. This is the format of simevent::simulate_events().

models

A list with the hazard model of each event process: a formula such as death ~ biomarker + illness, naming the process on the left and its covariates on the right, or a hazard_model() to also restrict when individuals are at risk of it. Other processes can be used as covariates by name, giving their number of events so far, and the time of an event through an indicator such as I(event_time(illness, 1) > 0.5) (see hazard_model()), also in the censoring model. Every event in data needs a model, including the censoring process.

tau

Positive number. Follow-up horizon; the target parameters are evaluated at tau.

censoring

String. Name of the censoring process in models.

treatment_model

Optional logistic regression model for the baseline treatment, a two-sided formula such as treatment ~ biomarker. Required when arms is given.

arms

Integer vector of the baseline treatment values (0/1) to prepare interventional hazards and clever weights for. Each value can then be passed as a to tmle_estimate() and intervention_curve(). Defaults to both values, 0:1, when treatment_model is given.

max_count

Positive integer. Maximum number of jumps tracked per recurrent process in the state space.

control

A named list of tuning settings:

  • prune_states (FALSE): if TRUE, prune states not admissible under the at-risk conditions of models.

  • use_exponential (FALSE): if TRUE, always transform the hazard increments dH to probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise this is only done if some increments exceed 1.

hal_control

A named list of settings for processes fitted with fit = "hal", see Details.

cores

Positive integer. Number of cores used by parallel::mclapply() when predicting hazards across states.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print model fits and progress.

Value

An object of class initial_fit, a list with elements:

  • n: the number of individuals.

  • tau, treatment_model and arms: as given (arms with its default filled in).

  • models: the hazard models, as a list of hazard_model()s named by process.

  • processes: a data.table with one row per process and columns name, type ("terminal", "recurrent" or "one_jump", inferred from the data), model and at_risk (whether the process has a limit or at_risk condition).

  • cox_fits: the fitted survival::coxph() model of each process, named by process. A recurrent process z in a model is fitted as the indicators I(z >= 1) + ... + I(z >= max_count). as_sim_model() builds a simulation model from them.

It also contains the internal elements used by tmle_estimate(), among them tmp_long (the expanded data with fitted hazards and clever weights) and depend_matrix (the product state space).

Details

HAL fits are experimental and require a fit.hal() function to be available on the search path. hal_control may contain cut_time (35), cut_one_way (15), cut_tk (3), cut_tk_values (NULL), two_way (NULL), reduce_nk (0.025), sl (a list of HAL library specifications, built from cut_one_way, cut_tk, cut_tk_values and two_way by default), screen_two_way (FALSE), lambda_cvs, event_dependent_cv (FALSE), npenalize_vars (NULL), v_folds (10), seed (NULL), reduce_seed_dependence (FALSE), penalize_time (FALSE) and verbose (FALSE), with defaults in parentheses.

Columns of data named after a process, such as the event counts that simevent::simulate_events() adds, are ignored: the counts are recomputed from event.

Examples

# Illness-death data: illness is an illness that can occur once, death ends
# follow-up, and so does censoring. One row per event:
head(illness_death)
#>   id      time     event  biomarker treatment
#> 1  1 2.8926838 censoring  0.2724785         1
#> 2  2 0.1282264   illness  0.3572619         0
#> 3  2 1.2558891     death  0.3572619         0
#> 4  3 0.6567113     death -0.8616620         0
#> 5  4 0.1752960   illness  0.8083350         1
#> 6  4 0.2409278     death  0.8083350         1

# One hazard model per process. The death hazard depends on whether the
# individual has fallen ill, and the illness can occur at most once:
fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  models = list(
    hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),
    death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,
    censoring ~ biomarker
  ),
  tau = 1
)
fit
#> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1
#> 
#>         name     type                                   model at_risk
#>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>
#> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE
#> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE
#> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE

# The process types are inferred from the data, and the hazard models are
# kept for reference:
fit$processes
#>         name     type                                   model at_risk
#>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>
#> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE
#> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE
#> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE
fit$models$death
#> Hazard model: death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness

# With a baseline treatment, a treatment model prepares estimates under
# both arms, for `a` in tmle_estimate():
fit_treated <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  models = list(
    hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),
    death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,
    censoring ~ biomarker
  ),
  tau = 1,
  treatment_model = treatment ~ biomarker
)
fit_treated
#> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1
#> 
#>         name     type                                   model at_risk
#>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl>
#> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE
#> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE
#> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE
#> 
#> Treatment model: treatment ~ biomarker, prepared for arms a = 0, 1

# \donttest{
# Data simulated with simevent can be passed as is. Here relapse is
# recurrent, and the death hazard grows with the number of relapses so far,
# tracked up to max_count:
if (requireNamespace("simevent", quietly = TRUE)) {
  model <- simevent::sim_model(
    biomarker = simevent::sim_covariate(function(N) rnorm(N)),
    relapse = simevent::sim_process("transient", eta = 0.6, nu = 1),
    death = simevent::sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),
    censoring = simevent::sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),
    effects = list(
      simevent::sim_effect(relapse ~ biomarker, coef = 0.5),
      simevent::sim_effect(death ~ relapse, coef = 0.4)
    )
  )
  relapses <- simevent::simulate_events(model, n = 200, seed = 1)

  fit_initial(
    relapses,
    models = list(
      relapse ~ biomarker,
      death ~ biomarker + relapse,
      censoring ~ biomarker
    ),
    tau = 2,
    max_count = 3
  )
}
#> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 2
#> 
#>         name      type                       model at_risk
#>       <char>    <char>                      <char>  <lgcl>
#> 1:   relapse recurrent         relapse ~ biomarker   FALSE
#> 2:     death  terminal death ~ biomarker + relapse   FALSE
#> 3: censoring  terminal       censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE
# }
